content.text: tutortrace uist camera ready due 8/14. rebuttal promised (1) cross-course analysis and (2) a limitations section. cross course is done (added CS2114 data, F1 drops a bit). need the limitations section now. reviewers flagged: label reliability (kappa .71, 3 raters), generalization beyond one course, privacy of telemetry. ~250 words

**Limitations**

*Label reliability.* Our labels come from three trained raters who reached Cohen's κ = 0.71 on a shared sample. This is substantial but not perfect agreement, and the hardest distinctions (e.g., stalling versus deliberate reading) remain partly subjective. Model performance is bounded by this ceiling, and we release the labeling guide so others can examine and refine our categories.

*Generalization.* Our main analysis uses one CS1 course at one institution. Our cross-course analysis on a second course (Section 6.4) shows a modest drop in performance, suggesting that some signals transfer while others depend on course-specific assignments and tooling. Courses with different languages, assignment structures, or assistant policies may behave differently, and we do not claim our thresholds apply unchanged elsewhere.

*Privacy of telemetry.* TutorTrace relies on fine-grained keystroke and run telemetry, which can reveal more about students than they expect. All data were collected with consent under an IRB-approved protocol and de-identified before analysis. Deployments outside research should limit retention, avoid using telemetry for grading, and make collection visible to students. We see the tool as support for instructor check-ins, not as surveillance.

*Labels as proxy.* Finally, rater labels describe observed behavior, not students' own experience. A window labeled as stalling may feel productive to the student. Future work should pair telemetry with student self-reports.

(~240 words)
"modest drop" — it went from 0.76 to 0.69. is modest fair

A 0.07 drop is more than "modest" to many readers. Safer to give the number and let it speak:

> Our cross-course analysis on a second course (Section 6.4) shows macro-F1 decreasing from 0.76 to 0.69, suggesting that some signals transfer while others depend on course-specific assignments and tooling.

Reviewers who asked about generalization will appreciate the number more than the adjective.
ok fits in 10 pages still? we're at 9.8 lol

At 9.8 pages you have room for the extra clause, barely. If it pushes over, the cheapest cut is usually in related work: one sentence of overlap with the intro, or a citation list that can lose a "see also". Don't cut from the limitations section; that's the part the reviewers asked for.
